issues.label: Extension of time for leave to appeal: error by Board member
Leave to appeal: error by Board member
Remedy: set aside and remit to different Board member
Procedural fairness: ex parte decision and Board procedures

result.overall: The Court set aside the Board member's decision granting an extension of time and leave to appeal, finding the extension was granted without a principled approach and unsupported by evidence, and remitted the matter for redetermination by a different Board member.

themes.name: Extension of time criteria
themes.summary: The Court emphasized that extensions of time are not automatic and must be granted based on established criteria, including explanation for delay and prejudice to the other party.

themes.name: Procedural fairness and Board process
themes.summary: The Court noted concerns about the ex parte nature of the Board's decision and the lack of reasons, but declined to require procedural changes.

themes.name: Standard of review
themes.summary: The Court assumed without deciding the standard of review, finding the decision unreasonable on any standard.

themes.name: Remedy and directions on remittal
themes.summary: The Court set aside the decision and provided guidance for the Board on remittal, specifying the factors to be considered.

arguments.quote: The Minister alleges that the member designate of the Board erred in granting (a) an extension of time and (b) leave to appeal.
arguments.claim: The Board member erred in granting both an extension of time and leave to appeal.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court agreed the member erred in extending time, which was dispositive.

arguments.quote: the Applicant submits that, in spite of this discretionary nature of the decision, I should apply a standard of review of reasonableness simpliciter (Callihoo v. Canada, [2000] F.C.J. No. 612 (T.D.))
arguments.claim: The standard of review should be reasonableness simpliciter.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court did not decide the standard of review, finding the decision unreasonable on any standard.

arguments.quote: Her reasons, as set out in her initial letter to the Board dated February 8, 2004, were as follows: Ms. Gattellaro did not act earlier on this due to many difficulties in her life.
arguments.claim: The delay was due to depression, marital problems, raising young children, lack of understanding of the process, and abandonment by her representative.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court found these reasons unsupported by the evidence and inconsistent with the record.
arguments.gap: No affidavit or supporting evidence provided on judicial review.

arguments.quote: No reasons were provided. Further, the decision was taken ex parte, without notice to or submissions from the Minister.
arguments.claim: The Board's ex parte decision and lack of reasons was procedurally unfair.
arguments.outcome_note: The Court noted the concern but declined to require procedural changes.

holdings.quote: I do not need to reach a conclusion on the appropriate standard since I am satisfied that, on any standard of review, the decision should not stand.
holdings.statement: The Court assumed without deciding the standard of review, finding the decision unreasonable on any standard.

holdings.quote: The authority to extend the statutory limitation must not, in my view, be exercised arbitrarily or capriciously.
holdings.statement: Extensions of time under s. 83(1) CPP must not be granted arbitrarily or capriciously.

holdings.quote: the following criteria must be considered and weighed: 1. A continuing intention to pursue the application or appeal; 2. The matter discloses an arguable case; 3. There is a reasonable explanation for the delay; and 4. There is no prejudice to the other party in allowing the extension.
holdings.statement: The Grewal criteria apply to extensions of time under s. 83(1) CPP: intention, arguable case, explanation for delay, and prejudice.

holdings.quote: Provided that the record demonstrates that there was a reasonable evidentiary basis upon which the member could assess the factors, it would not be up to this Court to re-weigh the evidence.
holdings.statement: The Court will not re-weigh evidence if the record shows a reasonable evidentiary basis for the Board's assessment.

holdings.quote: I am prepared to assume, without deciding, that the first two criteria have been met. However, I have serious concerns with respect to the last two factors of explanation for the delay and prejudice to the Minister.
holdings.statement: The Court found the explanation for delay and consideration of prejudice to the Minister lacking.

holdings.quote: A conclusion that the Respondent has provided compelling or sufficient reasons for bringing the leave application seven years after the 90-day time limit of s. 83(1) is, in my view, totally unsupported by the evidence and is patently unreasonable.
holdings.statement: The Board member's finding of sufficient reasons for delay was unsupported and unreasonable.

holdings.quote: the record discloses no evidence whatsoever on the question of prejudice to the Minister. It does not appear that prejudice to the Minister was considered by the member.
holdings.statement: The Board failed to consider prejudice to the Minister.

holdings.quote: An application for an extension of time - particularly for seven years beyond the statutory time limit - should not be granted as a matter of right, but should be subjected to a principled approach by the Board. In this case, that was not done.
holdings.statement: The Board failed to apply a principled approach to the extension of time request.

holdings.quote: The decision under review will be set aside and the matter referred back to the Board for re-determination, having regard to these reasons, by a different member of the Board.
holdings.statement: The decision is set aside and remitted to a different Board member for redetermination in accordance with the Court's reasons.

holdings.quote: the member designated to consider the application for the extension of time should satisfy himself that: _ The Respondent demonstrates a continuing intention to pursue the application or appeal; _ The matter discloses an arguable case; _ There is a reasonable explanation for the delay; and _ There is no prejudice to the Minister in allowing the extension.
holdings.statement: On remittal, the Board must consider and be satisfied of all four Grewal criteria.

holdings.quote: I recognize that the Board is the master of its own procedures and, therefore, decline to require the Board to implement procedures that would address these shortcomings.
holdings.statement: The Court declined to require the Board to change its procedures regarding ex parte decisions.

holdings.quote: In my discretion, I decline to award costs in this application.

rebuttals.quote: A review of the record demonstrates that her reasons do not hold up to scrutiny.
rebuttals.point: The delay was due to depression, marital problems, raising young children, lack of understanding of the process, and abandonment by her representative.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court found these reasons unsupported by the evidence and inconsistent with the record.

rebuttals.quote: It is difficult to see how the Board can reach a fair, principled decision on these applications on an ex parte basis; that is, without the submissions from the Minister. In spite of this concern, I recognize that the Board is the master of its own procedures and, therefore, decline to require the Board to implement procedures that would address these shortcomings.
rebuttals.point: The Board's ex parte decision and lack of reasons was procedurally unfair.
rebuttals.court_answer: The Court noted the concern but declined to require procedural changes.
